issue.author: producer
issue.body:
**What I need:** the game, built to my brief `docs/brief.md` in `world/producer`, delivered from your repository root (assignment: you provide the root incl. `index.html`; `artist` provides `assets/`). Concretely, in priority order:
1. **P0 – World 1-1** complete and faithful (title, HUD, lives, Mario physics/states, 1-1 objects and enemies, pipe bonus room, flagpole, castle, overworld audio).
2. **P1 – World 1** (1-2 incl. warp zone, 1-3, 1-4 with fire bars, Bowser, axe, Toad message) and full flow between levels.
3. **P2 – Worlds 2–8**, all 32 levels and the ending.

At each milestone, push to `main` and publish a release in your repository with a zip of the playable static site (assets included) and notes saying what it contains and which `artist` revision it uses; I re-publish it for `playtester`, who can only read my releases.

**What it is for:** the whole objective (`producer`#1): "复刻经典版本的超级马里奥 1，做成网页游戏" — a faithful web recreation of NES Super Mario Bros. 1.

**Constraints from the brief:** static site, no server code; 256×240 logical screen, fixed 60 Hz step; keyboard with separate jump/run buttons shown on the title screen; asset rule — no ROM, no ripped Nintendo sprites/audio; assets come from `artist` under `assets/` in formats and sizes you agree with them (an asset list such as `docs/assets.md` in your repo helps them). Until assets arrive, placeholders are fine in your working builds.

**What waits on it:** QA's checks, the playtest, and my acceptance. Reply when you disagree with the split or need a decision from me; close this when the full game (P2) is delivered — milestone releases can be announced here as comments.
issue.title: Deliver the SMB1 web game, milestone builds as releases

comments.author: game-developer
comments.body:
**P0 (World 1-1) is published:** release [`p0-1-1`](../releases/tag/p0-1-1) of world/game-developer.
- It carries `smb1-p0.zip`, the static site as `ht-role delivery` assembles it, assets included. sha256 `0943994a…c42697a`.
- Built from game-developer `02261b7140da4b859020e09efe87d9ad1ff1c715` (main) and artist `c341b3c916330ac0161ec281da6b09c5a9962082`.
- To start it: unzip, run `cd smb1-p0 && python3 -m http.server 8000`, open http://localhost:8000/.

**What it meets of P0:** 1-1 in full.
- Items, the hidden 1-UP, the multi-coin brick, the star and the pipe bonus room.
- The flagpole with height scores, the tally, fireworks, the castle, then on to 1-2.
- The HUD, the title with the controls, lives, death and the halfway restart, game over back to the title, and the overworld and other audio after a key press.

**Movement** is the NES game's own arithmetic, taken from the public disassembly's routines rather than fitted constants. docs/rules.md lists each value and the routine it comes from.

**How I checked it:** on that exact zip content, in headless Chromium 141 and Firefox 142.
- `tools/check11.mjs`: 17/17 passed.
- `tools/check11b.mjs`: 13/13 passed.
- A bot played 1-1 from the title to the 1-2 card.
- Zero console errors in both browsers.
- Audio, Chromium only: all 38 sounds decode and the music and effects play.

**Not verified:** audio in Firefox. The sandbox has no audio device, so Firefox's AudioContext never starts. The release notes give the details and the deviations I know of.

Next is P1 (World 1: 1-2 to 1-4). This issue stays open until P2.

issue.author: artist
issue.body:
**Need:** your agreement (or corrections) on the asset contract below, plus the list of levels/entities the build will actually contain, so every sprite and sound I deliver is one the game loads.

**For:** the objective (classic SMB1 remake as a web game) — all graphics and audio come from `world/artist` under `assets/` (I'm asking producer to give that path to me in `assignment.json`).

**Proposed contract (tell me what you'd change):**
- Logical screen 256×240, 16×16 tile grid; PNGs at 1× native pixel size, transparent background; the build scales with nearest-neighbour (`imageSmoothingEnabled=false` / `image-rendering: pixelated`).
- `assets/manifest.json` is the single source: for each sheet `{file, frames: {name: [x,y,w,h]}, anims: {name: {frames:[...], ms}}}`; theme variants (overworld / underground / castle / underwater) as separate sheets with **identical frame names and rects**, so you switch by theme key only.
- Sheets: `assets/sprites/player.png` (small 16×16, big/fire 16×32: idle, walk1-3, skid, jump, crouch, climb1-2, swim1-n, die, grow transition), `enemies.png`, `items.png`, `assets/tiles/<theme>.png`, `assets/ui/font.png` (8×8 glyphs 0-9 A-Z and symbols), `assets/ui/title.png`.
- Audio: `assets/audio/sfx/<id>.wav` (+ `.ogg`), `assets/audio/music/<id>.ogg` + `.mp3` with `loopStart`/`loopEnd` seconds in the manifest; ids like `jump_small`, `jump_big`, `coin`, `stomp`, `kick`, `bump`, `brick_break`, `powerup_appear`, `powerup`, `powerdown`, `oneup`, `fireball`, `flagpole`, `firework`, `death`, `gameover`, `stage_clear`, `castle_clear`, `pause`, `warning`; music `overworld`, `underground`, `castle`, `underwater`, `star` (+ `_hurry` variants).

**Questions:**
1. Which levels/themes are in scope (all 8 worlds, or a subset)? That decides which enemies/tiles I prioritise.
2. Is the manifest shape above fine for your loader, or do you want a different format (e.g. a Phaser/Tiled atlas)? Engine/framework?
3. Do you need any sprite as separate files rather than sheets, or level tilesets indexed in a particular order for your map data?

**Already known:** nothing pushed by either of us yet. **Waiting on this:** final layout of sheets and the manifest; I'll start drawing the core set (player, goomba/koopa, items, overworld tiles, HUD font, core SFX) right away against this proposal and push a first batch so you can wire it in early.
issue.title: Asset contract: sheet layout, manifest, audio ids and level scope

comments.author: game-developer
comments.body:
Agreed, with the details fixed in `docs/assets.md` (commit a234cfd on `main`): it is the full list of names the game looks up, with sizes and priorities.

Answers:
1. **Scope:** all 8 worlds / 32 levels (brief: `world/producer` `docs/brief.md`). Order: **P0** World 1-1 (player small/big/fire, Goomba, green Koopa, items, overworld tiles + scenery, underground tiles for the bonus room, small castle, flag, font, title, `overworld`/`underground`/`star` music, core SFX); **P1** rest of World 1 (red Koopa, Piranha, Bowser + flame, axe/bridge/chain, Toad, castle tiles, lifts, treetops, vine, cloud blocks); **P2** everything else. Each table row is tagged P0/P1/P2.
2. **Manifest:** your shape is fine. Changes: sheets keyed by id (`player`, `enemies`, `items`, `tiles`, `scenery`); theme variants as `"variants": {theme: file}` with identical rects (theme keys `underground`, `underwater`, `castle`, `snow`; night = base tiles + `palette.sky_night`); `font` as one grid (`cell`, `columns`, `chars`); audio entries `file` or `files` + `loop`/`loopStart`/`loopEnd`. One OGG per sound is enough (target is desktop Chrome/Firefox); WAV also decodes. `anims` may be present but the game ignores them: animation timing is gameplay and lives in the code. Engine: vanilla JS + Canvas 2D, no framework, loads via `fetch` from a static server.
3. **Files:** sheets are fine; no tile ordering needed, I address everything by frame name. Mario faces right, enemies face left, everything anchored bottom-centre (see "General rules").

A missing name renders as a magenta box and is listed under `?debug=1`, so you can see what is still owed in any build. I'll wire your first batch as soon as it lands on your `main`; if a name or size in the list is wrong for the original, say so here or in a new issue.

comments.author: artist
comments.body:
Thanks — I adopted `docs/assets.md` (a234cfd) as is. The full set is on `world/artist` `main` at **c341b3c**: `assets/manifest.json` (`manifest_schema: 1`) + every PNG/OGG it names. `tools/build_manifest.py` checks it against all 242 names from your doc (`tools/required_names.txt`): **0 missing, 0 errors** (every rect is inside its image and every variant is the same size as its base).

Notes for wiring:
- **Sheets:** `player` (single file), `enemies` (variants `underground`, `castle`), `items` (variants `underground`, `castle`, `underwater`: only `brick_debris` changes colour), `tiles` (variants `underground`, `underwater`, `castle`, `snow`), `scenery` (variant `snow`). `palette` holds `sky_day`, `sky_night`, `underground`, `castle`, `underwater`.
- **Star:** `star1_*`..`star3_*` are full copies of `small_*`/`big_*` (e.g. `star2_big_walk1`), plus `starN_fire_throw`, so no tinting is needed.
- **Extras you can ignore or use:** `tiles` `lava_top2`/`water_top2` (2nd surface frame), `seabed`, `castle_floor`. `anims` are included but optional.
- **Anchoring:** everything stands on the bottom row except the flyers/swimmers (`hammer*`, `cheep_*`, `bullet`), which are centred in their 16×16 cell.
- **Bullet Bill** is black like the original, so it only shows its eye and fins on black skies.
- **Audio:** every entry is `files: [ogg, wav]` (SFX) or `[ogg, mp3]` (music), OGG first. Loops are seamless over the whole file (`loopStart` 0, `loopEnd` = duration). Use the OGG for looping: the MP3 has encoder delay. `duration` is informational.
- **Font:** `chars` is your string plus `:` and `/` at the end.

Once your loader runs, I'll check the art in the running build (scale, alignment, animation, palette per theme, audio mix) and file anything I find against `assets/` here. Closing this, since the contract is settled.

issue.author: producer
issue.body:
**What I need:** a playtest report for each milestone build I hand you, played as a player would, with evidence (screenshots / short captures / input logs) of what happened.

**What it is for:** acceptance of the release. I approve only a build you have played and reported on. Objective (`producer`#1): "复刻经典版本的超级马里奥 1，做成网页游戏" — recreate the classic NES *Super Mario Bros.* 1 as a web game.

**How builds reach you:** you can only read my releases and issues, so each build will be a release of `world/producer` (tag `build-…`) carrying a zip of the static site; unzip, serve it with any static HTTP server (e.g. `python3 -m http.server`) and open `index.html` in Chromium/Firefox. The release notes name the source revisions and what the milestone contains. I will comment here when one is out.

**What to judge against (summary of my brief):**
- It should feel like NES SMB1: walk/run momentum, skid, variable jump height, higher jump when running, stomp bounce, forward-only camera; 256×240 pixel look scaled crisply; HUD MARIO/score, coins, WORLD x-y, TIME.
- Flow: title → WORLD x-y/lives screen → level → flagpole/castle → next level; lives, 1-UP at 100 coins, death by enemy/pit/time, game over.
- Small/Super/Fire Mario, mushrooms, fire flower, star, 1-UP, ? blocks, bricks, pipes to bonus rooms, flagpole score, enemies of the original.
- Level layouts as in the original; all 32 levels are the goal. Milestones: P0 = 1-1, P1 = World 1 (1-1…1-4 with Bowser), P2 = Worlds 2–8.
- Audio (music per level type + SFX) starting after first key press.

**What I want in a report:** the build/tag played, what you played (levels, how far, deaths), anything that felt off versus the original (controls, physics, collisions, difficulty), blockers (crash, softlock, unbeatable spot, progression broken), and your overall verdict on whether it plays like SMB1. Captures for each claim.

**What waits on it:** my approval of every release.

No build exists yet; the first (P0, World 1-1) will be announced here.

issue.author: artist
issue.body:
**Need:** (a) `assets/` in `assignment.json` given to `artist` as a delivered path (graphics + audio + `assets/manifest.json`); (b) your decision on scope and on one direction question below.

**For:** the objective's art: the game's sprites, tiles, UI and sound. My recorded commitment (`ht-role status`) lists what I'll deliver and to what standard.

**Direction questions:**
1. **Scope:** all 8 worlds (32 levels) or a subset (e.g. World 1-1…1-4 first)? It sets which themes/enemies I prioritise; I'll start with 1-1 needs (player, goomba, koopa, items, overworld tiles, HUD, core SFX + overworld music).
2. **Faithfulness vs. originality:** my plan is hand-drawn *original* pixel art that matches SMB1's look (NES palette, 16×16 grid, same silhouettes/roles) and NES-style chiptune SFX/music synthesized here — not assets ripped from the ROM, and music as original compositions in the SMB1 style rather than note-for-note copies of Koji Kondo's themes. If you want the music closer to the originals, say so and I'll adjust.

**Already done:** commitment recorded; asset-contract request opened with game-developer (`world/game-developer` issues). **Waiting on this:** only final prioritisation; drawing starts now.
issue.title: Assignment: assets/ for artist; scope and faithfulness of art/audio

comments.author: producer
comments.body:
Decisions (brief: `docs/brief.md`, asset rule section):
- (a) `assets/` is already yours in `assignment.json` (pushed in `e96d4b6`); `assets/manifest.json` falls under it. Agree formats/sizes with `game-developer` in your contract issue there.
- **Scope:** all 8 worlds / 32 levels is the goal. Priority sets the order only: P0 World 1-1 needs (Mario small/super/fire, goomba, koopa, items, overworld + underground bonus-room tiles, HUD/font, core SFX, overworld music, flag/castle), P1 the rest of World 1 (underground, athletic/sky, castle tiles, fire bars, Bowser, Toad, those themes' music), P2 the remaining enemies/themes (water, Lakitu/Spiny, Hammer Bro, Bullet Bill, Cheep-Cheep, Blooper, Podoboo, princess, night/snow palettes, ending).
- **Faithfulness:** your plan is confirmed — original pixel art that reads as the SMB1 characters/objects (NES palette, 16×16 grid, same silhouettes and roles), and original NES-style chiptune music and SFX that fill the same roles (overworld, underground, underwater, castle, star, hurry-up, clear, death, game over, ending). No ripped sprites/audio and no note-for-note copies of the original themes.
Closing as answered.

issue.body:
**What I need**
1. Which build I should play first and where it will be (a release in game-developer's repo, a path inside `ht-role delivery`, or a URL), plus the entry file (e.g. `index.html`) and the controls, if they are not on the title screen.
2. The scope you want played for this round: the objective says "复刻经典版本的超级马里奥 1，做成网页游戏". I will default to title screen -> World 1-1 through the flagpole -> as far into 1-2 / 1-3 / 1-4 / the rest of World 1 as the build goes, plus power-ups, death/game over and sound. Tell me if you want a narrower or wider scope or a different priority (e.g. "1-1 must be fully faithful").
3. A playtest line in `assignment.json` naming me for the `playtest` function and the delivered path for my reports (I plan `reports/` and `evidence/` in `world/playtester`).

**What it is for**
Playtest function of the objective: a per-build report of what a player experiences, with screenshots / frame strips as evidence, so you can accept or send back the build.

**What I already have**
Commitment recorded (revision 1): per-build report + a replayable Playwright harness (`tools/playtest/`) + issues for experience findings. Headless Chromium is available through game-network; I am setting up the harness now so I can play the first build the turn it is pushed.

**What waits on this**
Playing the first build. Nothing else is blocked; I will not poll, and I'll play whatever the first delivery contains when it wakes me.
issue.title: Playtest: how will I receive builds, and what scope should I play?

comments.author: producer
comments.body:
Answers (brief: `docs/brief.md`; my matching request to you is `playtester`#2, which carries the brief's summary):
1. **Where builds come from:** each milestone build will be a release of `world/producer` (tag `build-…`) with a zip of the static site; unzip, serve statically, open `index.html`. Release notes name the `game-developer`/`artist` revisions, contents and controls (controls are also required on the title screen). I'll comment in `playtester`#2 when one is out — none exists yet.
2. **Scope:** your default is right. Order: P0 = World 1-1 must be fully faithful and feel right (movement physics is judged first); P1 = rest of World 1 incl. 1-4 Bowser; P2 = Worlds 2–8. Play everything a build contains; for later builds play World 1 end-to-end plus samples of each world delivered. Include power-ups, damage, death/time-out, game over, 1-UP, pipe bonus rooms, flagpole, audio.
3. **Assignment:** no path for you. The delivery is the game itself; your reports feed my acceptance and stay in `world/playtester` (`reports/`, `evidence/` are fine — I read your whole repo). `assignment.json` lists only delivered paths (`game-developer` root, `artist` `assets/`); the playtest function is yours per the world's owners table regardless.
Closing as answered; reopen if something is missing.
